messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and for a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a thorough cleaning (strings, fretboard, body). Replace old strings if needed. | A well‑maintained instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture the whole body, headstock, neck, fretboard, and any visible wear or damage. Use natural light and a neutral background. | Good photos attract buyers and reduce the chance of disputes over condition. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local classifieds. Look at similar models, age, and condition. | Knowing the going rate helps you price competitively and avoid underselling. | | **4. Write a Detailed Description** | Include brand, model, year, serial number, string gauge, any modifications, and a brief history. Mention any flaws honestly. | Transparency builds trust and reduces returns or disputes. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform(s)** | • **Reverb** – great for musical instruments, buyer protection.
• **eBay** – wide audience, auction or fixed price.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local Music Stores / Pawn Shops** – quick sale, but usually lower price.
• **Consignment Shops** – they handle sales, but take a commission. | Different platforms reach different audiences; use multiple if you’re not in a hurry. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | Start slightly above your target price to allow room for negotiation. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a higher starting point can still land you a good deal. | | **7. Decide on Shipping vs. Local Pickup** | • **Shipping**: Use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and a reputable carrier (UPS, FedEx, USPS). Offer tracking and insurance.
• **Pickup**: Meet in a safe, public place (coffee shop, library). Bring a friend if possible. | Shipping expands your buyer pool but adds cost; pickup saves money but limits reach. | | **8. Secure Payment** | • **Online**: PayPal Goods & Services, Venmo (with caution), or bank transfer.
• **In‑person**: Cash or debit card. Verify funds before handing over the guitar. | Protect yourself from fraud and ensure you receive payment before delivery. | | **9. Handle Negotiations Professionally** | Keep communication polite, respond promptly, and be prepared to justify your price with photos and market data. | Good rapport can lead to a quicker sale and a better price. | | **10. Finalize the Sale** | Once payment is confirmed, ship or hand over the guitar. Provide a receipt or confirmation email. | Documentation protects both parties and satisfies any platform policies. | ### Quick Tips & Common Pitfalls | Tip | Explanation | |-----|-------------| | **Avoid “Too Good to Be True” Offers** | If someone offers far above market value, verify their legitimacy. | | **Use a Case** | Even a simple gig bag can protect the guitar during transport. | | **Check Serial Number** | Buyers may want to confirm authenticity; keep it handy. | | **Offer a Return Window** | Some platforms allow a short return period; this can increase buyer confidence. | | **Keep Records** | Save all communications, receipts, and shipping labels. | ### Example Listing (Reverb) ``` Title: 2015 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition Description: - Brand/Model: Yamaha FG800 - Year: 2015 - Serial #: 12345678 - Neck: 25.5" scale, 20 frets - Body: Solid spruce top, mahogany back & sides - Strings: New set of D’Addario EJ16 (12–56) - Condition: Minor light scratches on the back, no cracks - Extras: Included gig bag, strap, and a set of replacement strings Price: $350 (fixed) Photos: [Attach 8 high‑resolution images] Shipping: Free worldwide shipping via UPS Ground, insured, with tracking. Payment: PayPal Goods & Services (buyer pays shipping). ``` Feel free to adapt the template to your own guitar’s specifics. Good luck with your sale!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "How can I sell my acoustic guitar?" They want advice. We can provide steps: research market value, clean instrument, take photos, list on platforms (eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, Reverb), set price, describe condition, shipping options, safety tips. Also mention local music stores, pawn shops, consignment. Provide tips for negotiation, payment methods, etc. No need to call function.
